title: AI-native product design: patterns for autonomy, trust and exceptions
thesis: AI-native products differ from AI-enhanced ones by making automation the default and putting humans on exceptions; trust is earned through visible confidence, explanations and easy reversal, not through chat interfaces.
audience: Product designers and PMs building AI features into SaaS

questions.question: What guidelines and patterns exist for human-AI interaction design?
How should levels of automation and autonomy be chosen, and where do humans handle exceptions?
queries: human in the loop exception handling AI

questions.question: What builds or erodes appropriate trust in AI systems: explanations, confidence, overreliance?
Is chat the right interface? Evidence on conversational versus graphical and embedded AI interfaces
queries: chat interface limitations LLM user experience
conversational versus graphical user interface study

questions.question: How do AI-native products (Ramp, Linear, Notion, Vercel) design their AI features, according to their own teams?
